message.content:
Snowflake Inc. (CIK 1640147) remained loss-making on a GAAP basis in every fiscal year in the database, but its profitability improved markedly from FY2019 through FY2024 and then deteriorated in FY2025. All figures below are annual (fiscal years ending January 31), in USD, from 10-K filings.

**Net loss and net margin (net loss ÷ revenue, derived)**

| Fiscal year (end) | Revenue | Net loss | Net margin |
|---|---|---|---|
| FY2019 (2019-01-31) | $96.7M | –$178.0M | –184.2% |
| FY2020 (2020-01-31) | $264.7M | –$348.5M | –131.6% |
| FY2021 (2021-01-31) | $592.0M | –$539.1M | –91.1% |
| FY2022 (2022-01-31) | $1,219.3M | –$679.9M | –55.8% |
| FY2023 (2023-01-31) | $2,065.7M | –$796.7M | –38.6% |
| FY2024 (2024-01-31) | $2,806.5M | –$836.1M | –29.8% |
| FY2025 (2025-01-31) | $3,626.4M | –$1,285.6M | –35.5% |

**Operating margin (operating loss ÷ revenue, derived)**: –191.9% (FY2019), –135.3% (FY2020), –91.9% (FY2021), –58.6% (FY2022), –40.8% (FY2023), –39.0% (FY2024), –40.2% (FY2025). Operating loss widened in absolute terms every year, from –$185.5M to –$1,456.0M, but fell sharply as a share of revenue until FY2024.

**Interpretation**
- FY2019–FY2024: a clear, monotonic improvement in profitability ratios. Revenue grew roughly 29x while the net loss grew only about 4.7x, so the net margin narrowed by about 154 percentage points (from –184.2% to –29.8%). The operating margin improved by about 153 points over the same span. The company was scaling toward breakeven without reaching it.
- FY2025: the trend reversed. Revenue grew 29.2% to $3,626.4M, but the net loss jumped 53.8% to –$1,285.6M, widening the net margin by 5.7 points to –35.5%; the operating margin slipped 1.2 points to –40.2%. The pretax loss also widened to –$1,285.1M (fact 2506842), so the deterioration was operating-driven rather than tax-driven — the company carries a large valuation allowance ($3.1B at 2025-01-31) against its deferred tax assets, per the FY2025 10-K.

**Caveats**
- These are GAAP measures; Snowflake also reports non-GAAP operating income, which is not used here and would show a different picture.
- The FY2025 reversal is a factual observation from the reported figures; the filings' MD&A discusses gross margin and operating-expense drivers, but I did not retrieve a specific management attribution for the FY2025 margin decline, so no causal claim is made.
- Figures are the latest applicable annual disclosures; earlier-year values were cross-checked across multiple 10-Ks and were consistent (e.g., FY2024 net loss –$836,097,000 appears identically in the FY2024 and FY2025 filings).

Sources: financial_facts IDs 2507770/2507773/2507782/2507795/2507808/2507821/2507831 (NetIncomeLoss), 2507965/2507968/2507977/2507990/2508003/2508016/2508026 (OperatingIncomeLoss), 2509651/2509654/2509663/2509676/2509689/2509702/2509712 (RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax), 2506842 (pretax loss), accession 0001640147-25-000052 (FY2025 10-K, filed 2025-03-21) and prior 10-Ks; FY2025 10-K valuation-allowance note (chunk 1640147/snow-20250131:503802).
